    """
    Read CSV and produce model parameters.

    CSV -> model parameter mapping (exact names used):
      - Product_ID                       -> products (list of strings)
      - Profit_Per_Unit                  -> profit[p] (float)

    Returns:
      dict with keys: products, profit, machA_req, machB_req, labor_req, material_req,
                      min_prod, max_demand,
                      Machine_A_capacity, Machine_B_capacity, Labor_hours_available, Raw_Material_available

    Validations performed:
      - All required columns exist
      - No missing values in required columns
      - No negative Profit_Per_Unit
      - No negative resource requirements (Machine_A_Hours_Req, Machine_B_Hours_Req, Labor_Hours_Req, Raw_Material_Units_Req)
      - For every product: Min_Production_Requirement <= Max_Market_Demand

    Note: The capacity placeholders at module top are included in the returned dict; change them there as needed.
    """
    import pandas as pd

    # Required column names (must match CSV exactly)
    required_cols = [
        'Product_ID',
        'Profit_Per_Unit',
        'Machine_A_Hours_Req',
        'Machine_B_Hours_Req',
        'Labor_Hours_Req',
        'Raw_Material_Units_Req',
        'Min_Production_Requirement',
        'Max_Market_Demand'
    ]

    df = pd.read_csv(csv_path)

    # Check required columns
    missing_cols = [c for c in required_cols if c not in df.columns]
    if missing_cols:
        raise ValueError(f"CSV is missing required column(s): {missing_cols}")

    # Check for missing values in required columns
    null_cols = df[required_cols].isnull().any()
    cols_with_nulls = null_cols[null_cols].index.tolist() if null_cols.any() else []
    if cols_with_nulls:
        raise ValueError(f"Missing (NaN) values found in required column(s): {cols_with_nulls}")

    # Ensure numeric types where expected (raise if conversion fails)
    df['Profit_Per_Unit'] = pd.to_numeric(df['Profit_Per_Unit'], errors='raise')
    df['Machine_A_Hours_Req'] = pd.to_numeric(df['Machine_A_Hours_Req'], errors='raise')
    df['Machine_B_Hours_Req'] = pd.to_numeric(df['Machine_B_Hours_Req'], errors='raise')
    df['Labor_Hours_Req'] = pd.to_numeric(df['Labor_Hours_Req'], errors='raise')
    df['Raw_Material_Units_Req'] = pd.to_numeric(df['Raw_Material_Units_Req'], errors='raise')
    df['Min_Production_Requirement'] = pd.to_numeric(df['Min_Production_Requirement'], errors='raise')
    df['Max_Market_Demand'] = pd.to_numeric(df['Max_Market_Demand'], errors='raise')

    # Build products list (strings) and parameter dictionaries
    products = df['Product_ID'].astype(str).tolist()

    profit = dict(zip(products, df['Profit_Per_Unit'].astype(float).tolist()))
    machA_req = dict(zip(products, df['Machine_A_Hours_Req'].astype(float).tolist()))
    machB_req = dict(zip(products, df['Machine_B_Hours_Req'].astype(float).tolist()))
    labor_req = dict(zip(products, df['Labor_Hours_Req'].astype(float).tolist()))
    material_req = dict(zip(products, df['Raw_Material_Units_Req'].astype(float).tolist()))
    min_prod = dict(zip(products, df['Min_Production_Requirement'].astype(int).tolist()))
    max_demand = dict(zip(products, df['Max_Market_Demand'].astype(int).tolist()))

    # Validation: no negative profits
    neg_profits = {p: v for p, v in profit.items() if v < 0}
    if neg_profits:
        sample = list(neg_profits.items())[:10]
        raise ValueError(f"Negative Profit_Per_Unit found for products (sample up to 10): {sample}. Profits must be >= 0.")

    # Validation: no negative resource requirements

    for colname, d in [
        ('Machine_A_Hours_Req', machA_req),
        ('Machine_B_Hours_Req', machB_req),
        ('Labor_Hours_Req', labor_req),
        ('Raw_Material_Units_Req', material_req)

            messages.append(f"{col}: sample negatives {sample}")
        raise ValueError("Negative resource requirements found:\n" + "\n".join(messages) + "\nAll resource requirements must be >= 0.")

    # Validation: min_prod <= max_demand
    bad_bounds = [p for p in products if min_prod[p] > max_demand[p]]
    if bad_bounds:
        sample = bad_bounds[:10]
        raise ValueError(f"Products with Min_Production_Requirement > Max_Market_Demand (sample up to 10): {sample}. Fix bounds.")

    # Return a single dictionary ready for use in model building (PuLP or other)
    params = {
        'products': products,
        'profit': profit,
        'machA_req': machA_req,
        'machB_req': machB_req,
        'labor_req': labor_req,
        'material_req': material_req,
        'min_prod': min_prod,
        'max_demand': max_demand,
        # include capacity placeholders so caller can access or override them
        'Machine_A_capacity': Machine_A_capacity,
        'Machine_B_capacity': Machine_B_capacity,
        'Labor_hours_available': Labor_hours_available,
        'Raw_Material_available': Raw_Material_available
    }

    return params

    # Path to CSV (change if necessary). Using the Windows path from your input.

    machA_req = params['machA_req']

    solver = pulp.PULP_CBC_CMD(msg=True)

    status = pulp.LpStatus.get(prob.status, str(prob.status))
    total_profit = pulp.value(prob.objective)

    print('\nSolver status:', status)
    print(f'Total profit (objective): {total_profit}')

    # Gather produced units
    produced = {p: int(pulp.value(x[p])) if pulp.value(x[p]) is not None else 0 for p in products}

    # Only show produced_units > 0
    produced_positive = {p: q for p, q in produced.items() if q > 0}

        df_out = pd.DataFrame([{'Product': p, 'Produced_Units': q} for p, q in produced_positive.items()])

        print('\nProduced products (only > 0):')
        print(df_out.to_string(index=False))
    else:
        print('\nNo products produced in the optimal solution (all zero or infeasible).')

    # Resource usage and slack
    used_A = sum(machA_req[p] * produced[p] for p in products)
    used_B = sum(machB_req[p] * produced[p] for p in products)
    used_Labor = sum(labor_req[p] * produced[p] for p in products)
    used_Material = sum(material_req[p] * produced[p] for p in products)

    slack_A = Machine_A_capacity - used_A
    slack_B = Machine_B_capacity - used_B
    slack_Labor = Labor_hours_available - used_Labor
    slack_Material = Raw_Material_available - used_Material

    print('\nResource usage:')

    print(f" Raw_Mat:   used = {used_Material:.2f}  capacity = {Raw_Material_available:.2f}  slack = {slack_Material:.2f}")

    # If infeasible, print hint

    # End
